{"body":"Refs #2190.

PR #2190 moved every Git metadata consumer at once. The review exposed two separate jobs: define one owner for the metadata, then migrate its callers.

This is split part 1. It adds the resolver and changes only repository opening. Checkpoint, session, strategy, hooks, and other consumers stay unchanged here.

## Files and ownership

Three production files and four test files change. All paths below are relative to `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/`.

| File | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata.go` | No file | Resolves the three metadata facts |
| `repository.go` | Opening rediscovered paths | Resolves and passes metadata |
| `reftable.go` | Errors looked like absence | Returns inspection errors |
| `metadata_guard_test.go` | No guard | Blocks new duplicate traversal |
| `metadata_test.go` | No resolver tests | Covers real and broken layouts |
| `repository_test.go` | Tested the old path | Covers fallback and failures |
| `reftable_test.go` | Tested boolean detection | Covers inspection errors |

The call path changes like this:

```text
Before

OpenPath
  ├── resolve .git and commondir while opening
  ├── resolve them again while checking alternates
  └── fall back without one validated metadata result

After

OpenPath
  └── ResolveWorktreeMetadata
        ├── GitDir
        ├── CommonDir
        └── WorktreeID
              │
              ├── repository storage
              ├── alternates inspection
              └── reftable inspection
```

## One resolver for three facts

`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` resolves an explicit worktree root into:

- `GitDir`
- `CommonDir`
- `WorktreeID`

The resolver takes a worktree root. It does not discover one from CWD, read Git environment variables, run Git, cache results, or choose a caller's policy.

Resolution is all-or-error. Malformed or unreadable metadata stops the open.

`gitrepo.OpenPath` now resolves metadata once and passes those facts into repository opening, object-alternates detection, and reftable inspection.

A bare-repository open is tried only when worktree metadata does not exist.

## Symlinks and `..` keep their filesystem meaning

Lexically cleaning a path through a symlink can change where `..` leads. The resolver checks filesystem identity before it returns a cleaned path.

Linked-worktree registrations may use physical aliases. They must still resolve to an immediate child of `CommonDir/worktrees`.

Inspection errors now reach the caller. They no longer mean "feature absent." This applies to reftable inspection and malformed `.git` layouts.

## Fixes a hang that is already released

`OpenPath` on `main` identifies a `.git` entry by reading it: `os.Stat`, then `os.ReadFile`. That works for a directory or a regular file. For three other entry types the read never finishes.

| `.git` is | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A FIFO with no writer | Blocks until a writer opens it | Refused on type |
| A symlink to such a FIFO | Blocks until a writer opens it | Refused on type |
| A symlink to `/dev/zero` | Reads forever, memory grows | Refused on type |

The resolver checks the type first. It opens only a directory or a regular file, and refuses anything else by name.

None of these arrive by clone. Git refuses a `.git` path component in a tree at any depth, so each one needs local write access to the worktree. This is a robustness fix, not a vulnerability.

## `gitdir:` strictness now matches Git

The legacy parser accepted pointer files that Git rejects. It cut the prefix at `gitdir:` instead of `gitdir: `, then trimmed whitespace from the remainder. That let `gitdir:target`, ` gitdir: target`, and `gitdir:\ttarget` all resolve. Git requires the single space and trims nothing.
The fixture covers seven `.git` pointer spellings. The new resolver agrees with Git on all seven. The legacy parser agreed on three.
This changes behavior. A `.git` file that worked only because Entire was more permissive than Git now fails, and every other Git tool was already failing it.

## Stop new duplicate traversal

A source guard scans production Go across the repository. It rejects new `.git`, `gitdir:`, and `commondir` traversal outside `gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata`.
The guard lists the existing callers that later PRs must migrate:

- checkpoint metadata
- session metadata
- strategy and hooks
- remaining product consumers

The exception list records each function and the one `git rev-parse` flag it may use. If that function starts using another metadata flag, the guard fails. The test also fails when a listed exception no longer exists.

A temporary multi-file repository test runs the complete scanner. It proves that the scanner follows a package constant into another file, scans production code under `internal/`, and ignores a parameter named `gitDir`.

Positive controls cover rooted filesystem APIs, package constants, `Readlink`, aliased imports, and legacy resolver calls.

## Verification

- `mise run check`
  - formatting passed
  - lint passed with 0 issues
  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed
  - Vogon canary passed 56/56
  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4
- `git diff main --check`
- Real Git fixtures cover ordinary, linked, bare, separate-Git-dir, submodule, symlink-alias, moved-registration, alternates, and reftable layouts.
- On the seven `.git` pointer spellings in the fixture, the new resolver matches Git on 7/7. The legacy parser matched 3/7.
- Broken fixtures verify fail-closed repository opening and typed absence.

No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

## Deliberately not included

Checkpoint, session, strategy, hooks, and other product consumers still use their existing paths. Separate PRs will migrate them without mixing their error and fallback policies into this resolver change. The last migration will remove the legacy resolvers.

{"body":"> **Dependency:** This PR is built on #2241 and must not merge before it. Until #2241 lands, the Files changed view includes both #2241 and this checkpoint refactor. After #2241 merges, this branch will be rebased onto `main` and force-pushed so the PR contains only the checkpoint changes.

For the checkpoint-only change before that rebase, see the [comparison against the prerequisite branch](https://github.com/MuskanPaliwal/cli/compare/refactor-git-metadata-owner...refactor-checkpoint-metadata-resolution).

Refs #2052 and #2190.

PR #2190 established the broader direction: physical Git worktree metadata should have one canonical owner instead of being rediscovered independently across the CLI. PR #2241 introduces that owner in `gitrepo` and migrates repository opening. This PR follows it by moving the checkpoint subsystem onto the canonical metadata boundary and deleting checkpoint's duplicate traversal and caching implementation.

This is intended as an ownership refactor rather than a checkpoint behavior change. Queue placement, redaction caching, persistent refs, shadow refs, locking, and caller-specific failure policies remain intact.

## Broader refactor

Checkpoint operations need to know both the current worktree root and the repository's common Git directory. The common directory determines where repository-wide state such as the push queue and redaction cache belongs, particularly when a command runs from a linked worktree.

Before this change, checkpoint resolved that metadata itself:

```text
Checkpoint operation
        │
        ▼
checkpoint.resolveGitCommonDir
        │
        ├── git rev-parse --git-common-dir
        ├── package-level mutex
        └── per-worktree cache
```

That made checkpoint a second owner of the same physical Git facts already being consolidated under `gitrepo`. It also gave checkpoint its own cache lifecycle, cancellation-dependent behavior, and subprocess cost.

After this change, checkpoint starts from the already-open repository and delegates physical metadata resolution to the canonical owner:

```text
Checkpoint operation
        │
        ▼
checkpoint.repositoryDirs
        │
        ▼
gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata
        │
        ├── Worktree root
        ├── Per-worktree Git directory
        └── Common Git directory
```

The checkpoint package retains a small adapter because checkpoint callers commonly need the worktree root and common directory together. Interpretation of `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree layout remains owned exclusively by `gitrepo`.

## Why remove the checkpoint cache

The deleted cache was compensating for a Git subprocess rather than caching an expensive domain object. Once metadata resolution becomes rooted filesystem inspection, the cache no longer provides a useful ownership boundary.

Removing it has three useful consequences:

- An already-open repository no longer launches `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` when constructing checkpoint state.
- Repairs to `.git` or `commondir` metadata are observed by the next operation instead of remaining hidden behind a stale cached result.
- Checkpoint no longer owns a mutex, cache-clearing API, or cancellation-dependent cache semantics for facts owned by `gitrepo`.

This also removes the checkpoint-specific resolver and its cache-only tests.

## Checkpoint consumers moved to the canonical boundary

The migration covers the checkpoint paths that depend on repository metadata:

- rooted push-queue construction
- redaction-cache placement
- persistent ref updates
- ref-store construction
- ephemeral checkpoint storage
- shadow-ref operations
- file-lock placement

These consumers now receive metadata from the same resolver used when opening the repository, without introducing a generic Git facade or moving checkpoint-specific policy into `gitrepo`.

## Caller policy remains local

The canonical resolver reports metadata facts and errors; it does not decide whether an individual checkpoint feature is required or optional.

That distinction remains deliberate:

- Push-queue construction fails closed because enqueueing against the wrong repository directory could lose or misdirect required work.
- Redaction caching fails open because caching is an optimization and transcript redaction can continue without it.
- Persistent ref updates retain their existing locking, compare-and-swap conflict handling, retry, and cancellation behavior.
- Linked worktrees continue sharing repository-wide state through the common Git directory.
- Shadow refs and ephemeral checkpoint data retain their existing worktree-specific placement.

## Observable effect

No user-facing command or checkpoint format changes.

The operational effect is narrower:

- checkpoint metadata lookup no longer launches a Git subprocess for an already-open repository
- checkpoint metadata is no longer memoized independently from the filesystem
- malformed metadata continues to follow each caller's existing required or optional failure policy
- ordinary repositories and linked worktrees retain their existing storage locations

The checkpoint-only layer relative to #2241 contains 16 files, with 139 additions and 211 deletions. Most additions are focused behavioral tests; the production change primarily removes duplicate traversal and cache machinery.

## Verification

- `mise run check`
  - formatting passed
  - lint passed with 0 issues
  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed
  - Vogon canary passed 56/56
  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4
- Pre-PR `mise run lint` passed with 0 issues.
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check` passed.
- A real linked-worktree fixture proves that its queue is stored in the main repository's common Git directory.
- A repair test proves that corrected metadata is observed immediately without clearing a cache.
- A Git Trace2 test proves that constructing a checkpoint queue from an already-open repository launches no metadata Git subprocess.
- The Trace2 positive control runs `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and confirms that the subprocess detector records it.
- Tests preserve the required queue fail-closed and optional redaction-cache fail-open policies.
- The repository ownership guard no longer needs an exception for checkpoint metadata traversal.
- Source-built `entire status` passed.
- Source-built `entire doctor` reported metadata branches and hooks as healthy; it also found two pre-existing ended sessions awaiting condensation, unrelated to this diff.

No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

## Deliberately not included

This PR does not migrate session, strategy, hook, or other product consumers. Those areas have separate migrations so their error handling, fallback behavior, and performance-sensitive paths can be reviewed independently.

It also does not redesign checkpoint persistence, change ref formats, alter queue semantics, add cross-worktree writes, or replace genuine Git queries for refs, objects, configuration, and repository semantics.

{"body":"Refs #2052, particularly [the duplicate-traversal finding](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2052#issuecomment-5400538888) and [the follow-up commitment](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2052#issuecomment-5429341093).

PR #2052 exposed that several packages independently interpreted `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree identity. Those implementations had already diverged on layouts such as bare containers, linked worktrees, and submodules, while session and checkpoint maintained separate caches for answers derived from the same filesystem metadata.

This consolidates those physical Git facts under the existing `gitrepo` ownership boundary and removes the duplicate traversal and cache layers.

## Why this touches 67 files

This is one ownership change with a wide dependency graph, not 67 separate features.

Before this change, checkpoint, session, strategy, settings, status, review,
investigate, trail, setup/cleanup, and Codex independently interpreted some
combination of `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree identity:

```text
Before

checkpoint ─┐
session ────┤
strategy ───┤ each resolves Git metadata independently
settings ───┤ and some cache the result separately
status ─────┤
review ─────┤
Codex ──────┘

After

                    gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata
                                  │
              ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
           checkpoint          session            strategy...
```

The 67 changed files break down into 37 production files and 30 test files:

| Area | Files | Why they changed |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Canonical `gitrepo` owner | 7 | Add the resolver, repository-opening boundary, tests, and ownership guard |
| Checkpoint migration | 7 | Remove its common-directory cache and migrate consumers |
| Session migration | 7 | Remove its separate cache and preserve adoption/sweep behavior |
| Strategy and hook paths | 18 | Migrate the hottest and most policy-sensitive consumers |
| Other product consumers | 18 | Migrate settings, status, review, investigate, trail, Codex, setup, and cleanup |
| Legacy `paths` deletion | 2 | Remove the old marker-based worktree-ID parser |
| Cross-cutting proof | 8 | Update fixtures and prove caller policy and subprocess behavior |

Most production changes are small call-site migrations. The largest additions
are tests proving real Git layouts, failure behavior, ownership boundaries, and
subprocess counts. Despite the broad footprint, production Go decreases by 36
lines.

## One owner for physical worktree metadata

`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` now resolves one explicit worktree root into:

- its per-worktree Git directory
- its common Git directory
- its optional linked-worktree ID

The resolver has no CWD lookup, Git subprocess, cache, context, options, environment interpretation, layout taxonomy, or feature-specific policy.

Returned paths remain cleaned absolute lexical paths. Physical filesystem identity is used only to determine whether the Git directory equals the common directory and whether a linked-worktree Git directory is an immediate child of `CommonDir/worktrees`.

Resolution is all-or-error. Malformed worktree metadata cannot silently downgrade into another repository-opening path, while deliberately opening a validated bare repository remains a separate `gitrepo.OpenPath` operation.

## Consolidation and deletion

All former filesystem-metadata consumers now use the canonical resolver while retaining their existing caller-owned error, warning, fallback, trust, and installation policies.

This removes:

- the session common-directory cache and its clearing behavior
- the checkpoint common-directory cache
- duplicate `.git` and `commondir` traversal
- marker-based worktree-ID parsing
- the old `paths` worktree metadata helpers
- migration wrappers that would otherwise preserve fragmented ownership

A source guard rejects new production parsing of `gitdir:`, `commondir`, or independent `.git` filesystem traversal outside `gitrepo`, with two documented policy-only exceptions.

The production Go diff is 557 additions and 593 deletions: net 36 lines removed despite adding the canonical resolver.

## Hook-path subprocess evidence

Operation-level Git tracing records these changes against the historical pre-consolidation counts:

| Operation | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Session state construction | 2 | 1 |
| Construct and enqueue through checkpoint queue | 1 | 0 |
| `prepare-commit-msg` without an active session | 4 | 2 |
| `entire status` | 4 | 3 |
| Codex hook discovery | 1 | 1 |

These values count Git subprocesses, not whether the operation still occurs. The checkpoint queue retains its locking, append, drain, and removal behavior; it now obtains the common directory through filesystem metadata resolution instead of spawning Git.

The consolidation adds no Git subprocesses and removes the filesystem-metadata `--git-common-dir` queries. The one remaining common-directory query on the prepare-commit path is retained semantic repository-identity behavior rather than metadata traversal.

## Verification

- `mise run check`
  - formatting passed
  - lint passed with 0 issues
  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed
  - Vogon canary passed 56/56
  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`
- Real Git-created fixtures cover ordinary repositories, linked worktrees, `.bare/worktrees`, bare repositories with linked worktrees, separate Git directories, ordinary and linked submodules, relative pointers, symlink aliases, and moved registrations.
- Handmade fixtures cover malformed and broken metadata.
- Tests verify caller-owned failure policies, fail-closed repository opening, common-directory/worktree-ID agreement, and physical alias identity.
- The source guard was positive-control tested by temporarily adding forbidden independent traversal and observing the expected failure.
- No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

## Deliberately unchanged

This does not change Codex backlink, ownership, trust, warning, diagnostic, or installation policy. It does not add cross-worktree writes, resolver flags, a generic Git facade, or replace genuine Git queries for refs, objects, configuration, or repository semantics.

{"body":"Refs #2190.

PR #2190 moved every Git metadata consumer at once. The review exposed two separate jobs: define one owner for the metadata, then migrate its callers.

This is split part 1. It adds the resolver and changes only repository opening. Checkpoint, session, strategy, hooks, and other consumers stay unchanged here.

## Files and ownership

Three production files and four test files change. All paths below are relative to `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/`.

| File | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata.go` | No file | Resolves the three metadata facts |
| `repository.go` | Opening rediscovered paths | Resolves and passes metadata |
| `reftable.go` | Errors looked like absence | Returns inspection errors |
| `metadata_guard_test.go` | No guard | Blocks new duplicate traversal |
| `metadata_test.go` | No resolver tests | Covers real and broken layouts |
| `repository_test.go` | Tested the old path | Covers fallback and failures |
| `reftable_test.go` | Tested boolean detection | Covers inspection errors |

The call path changes like this:

```text
Before

OpenPath
  ├── resolve .git and commondir while opening
  ├── resolve them again while checking alternates
  └── fall back without one validated metadata result

After

OpenPath
  └── ResolveWorktreeMetadata
        ├── GitDir
        ├── CommonDir
        └── WorktreeID
              │
              ├── repository storage
              ├── alternates inspection
              └── reftable inspection
```

## One resolver for three facts

`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` resolves an explicit worktree root into:

- `GitDir`
- `CommonDir`
- `WorktreeID`

The resolver takes a worktree root. It does not discover one from CWD, read Git environment variables, run Git, cache results, or choose a caller's policy.

Resolution is all-or-error. Malformed or unreadable metadata stops the open.

`gitrepo.OpenPath` now resolves metadata once and passes those facts into repository opening, object-alternates detection, and reftable inspection.

A bare-repository open is tried only when worktree metadata does not exist.

## Symlinks and `..` keep their filesystem meaning

Lexically cleaning a path through a symlink can change where `..` leads. The resolver checks filesystem identity before it returns a cleaned path.

Linked-worktree registrations may use physical aliases. They must still resolve to an immediate child of `CommonDir/worktrees`.

Inspection errors now reach the caller. They no longer mean "feature absent." This applies to reftable inspection and malformed `.git` layouts.

## Fixes a hang that is already released

`OpenPath` on `main` identifies a `.git` entry by reading it: `os.Stat`, then `os.ReadFile`. That works for a directory or a regular file. For three other entry types the read never finishes.

| `.git` is | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A FIFO with no writer | Blocks until a writer opens it | Refused on type |
| A symlink to such a FIFO | Blocks until a writer opens it | Refused on type |
| A symlink to `/dev/zero` | Reads forever, memory grows | Refused on type |

The resolver checks the type first. It opens only a directory or a regular file, and refuses anything else by name.

None of these arrive by clone. Git refuses a `.git` path component in a tree at any depth, so each one needs local write access to the worktree. This is a robustness fix, not a vulnerability.

## `gitdir:` strictness now matches Git

The legacy parser accepted pointer files that Git rejects. It cut the prefix at `gitdir:` instead of `gitdir: `, then trimmed whitespace from the remainder. That let `gitdir:target`, ` gitdir: target`, and `gitdir:\ttarget` all resolve. Git requires the single space and trims nothing.
The fixture covers seven `.git` pointer spellings. The new resolver agrees with Git on all seven. The legacy parser agreed on three.
This changes behavior. A `.git` file that worked only because Entire was more permissive than Git now fails, and every other Git tool was already failing it.

## Stop new duplicate traversal

A source guard scans production Go across the repository. It rejects new `.git`, `gitdir:`, and `commondir` traversal outside `gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata`.
The guard lists the existing callers that later PRs must migrate:

- checkpoint metadata
- session metadata
- strategy and hooks
- remaining product consumers

The exception list records each function and the one `git rev-parse` flag it may use. If that function starts using another metadata flag, the guard fails. The test also fails when a listed exception no longer exists.

A temporary multi-file repository test runs the complete scanner. It proves that the scanner follows a package constant into another file, scans production code under `internal/`, and ignores a parameter named `gitDir`.

Positive controls cover rooted filesystem APIs, package constants, `Readlink`, aliased imports, and legacy resolver calls.

## Verification

- `mise run check`
  - formatting passed
  - lint passed with 0 issues
  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed
  - Vogon canary passed 56/56
  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4
- `git diff main --check`
- Real Git fixtures cover ordinary, linked, bare, separate-Git-dir, submodule, symlink-alias, moved-registration, alternates, and reftable layouts.
- On the seven `.git` pointer spellings in the fixture, the new resolver matches Git on 7/7. The legacy parser matched 3/7.
- Broken fixtures verify fail-closed repository opening and typed absence.

No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

## Deliberately not included

Checkpoint, session, strategy, hooks, and other product consumers still use their existing paths. Separate PRs will migrate them without mixing their error and fallback policies into this resolver change. The last migration will remove the legacy resolvers.

{"body":"> **Dependency:** This PR is built on #2241 and must not merge before it. Until #2241 lands, the Files changed view includes both #2241 and this checkpoint refactor. After #2241 merges, this branch will be rebased onto `main` and force-pushed so the PR contains only the checkpoint changes.

For the checkpoint-only change before that rebase, see the [comparison against the prerequisite branch](https://github.com/MuskanPaliwal/cli/compare/refactor-git-metadata-owner...refactor-checkpoint-metadata-resolution).

Refs #2052 and #2190.

PR #2190 established the broader direction: physical Git worktree metadata should have one canonical owner instead of being rediscovered independently across the CLI. PR #2241 introduces that owner in `gitrepo` and migrates repository opening. This PR follows it by moving the checkpoint subsystem onto the canonical metadata boundary and deleting checkpoint's duplicate traversal and caching implementation.

This is intended as an ownership refactor rather than a checkpoint behavior change. Queue placement, redaction caching, persistent refs, shadow refs, locking, and caller-specific failure policies remain intact.

## Broader refactor

Checkpoint operations need to know both the current worktree root and the repository's common Git directory. The common directory determines where repository-wide state such as the push queue and redaction cache belongs, particularly when a command runs from a linked worktree.

Before this change, checkpoint resolved that metadata itself:

```text
Checkpoint operation
        │
        ▼
checkpoint.resolveGitCommonDir
        │
        ├── git rev-parse --git-common-dir
        ├── package-level mutex
        └── per-worktree cache
```

That made checkpoint a second owner of the same physical Git facts already being consolidated under `gitrepo`. It also gave checkpoint its own cache lifecycle, cancellation-dependent behavior, and subprocess cost.

After this change, checkpoint starts from the already-open repository and delegates physical metadata resolution to the canonical owner:

```text
Checkpoint operation
        │
        ▼
checkpoint.repositoryDirs
        │
        ▼
gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata
        │
        ├── Worktree root
        ├── Per-worktree Git directory
        └── Common Git directory
```

The checkpoint package retains a small adapter because checkpoint callers commonly need the worktree root and common directory together. Interpretation of `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree layout remains owned exclusively by `gitrepo`.

## Why remove the checkpoint cache

The deleted cache was compensating for a Git subprocess rather than caching an expensive domain object. Once metadata resolution becomes rooted filesystem inspection, the cache no longer provides a useful ownership boundary.

Removing it has three useful consequences:

- An already-open repository no longer launches `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` when constructing checkpoint state.
- Repairs to `.git` or `commondir` metadata are observed by the next operation instead of remaining hidden behind a stale cached result.
- Checkpoint no longer owns a mutex, cache-clearing API, or cancellation-dependent cache semantics for facts owned by `gitrepo`.

This also removes the checkpoint-specific resolver and its cache-only tests.

## Checkpoint consumers moved to the canonical boundary

The migration covers the checkpoint paths that depend on repository metadata:

- rooted push-queue construction
- redaction-cache placement
- persistent ref updates
- ref-store construction
- ephemeral checkpoint storage
- shadow-ref operations
- file-lock placement

These consumers now receive metadata from the same resolver used when opening the repository, without introducing a generic Git facade or moving checkpoint-specific policy into `gitrepo`.

## Caller policy remains local

The canonical resolver reports metadata facts and errors; it does not decide whether an individual checkpoint feature is required or optional.

That distinction remains deliberate:

- Push-queue construction fails closed because enqueueing against the wrong repository directory could lose or misdirect required work.
- Redaction caching fails open because caching is an optimization and transcript redaction can continue without it.
- Persistent ref updates retain their existing locking, compare-and-swap conflict handling, retry, and cancellation behavior.
- Linked worktrees continue sharing repository-wide state through the common Git directory.
- Shadow refs and ephemeral checkpoint data retain their existing worktree-specific placement.

## Observable effect

No user-facing command or checkpoint format changes.

The operational effect is narrower:

- checkpoint metadata lookup no longer launches a Git subprocess for an already-open repository
- checkpoint metadata is no longer memoized independently from the filesystem
- malformed metadata continues to follow each caller's existing required or optional failure policy
- ordinary repositories and linked worktrees retain their existing storage locations

The checkpoint-only layer relative to #2241 contains 16 files, with 139 additions and 211 deletions. Most additions are focused behavioral tests; the production change primarily removes duplicate traversal and cache machinery.

## Verification

- `mise run check`
  - formatting passed
  - lint passed with 0 issues
  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed
  - Vogon canary passed 56/56
  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4
- Pre-PR `mise run lint` passed with 0 issues.
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check` passed.
- A real linked-worktree fixture proves that its queue is stored in the main repository's common Git directory.
- A repair test proves that corrected metadata is observed immediately without clearing a cache.
- A Git Trace2 test proves that constructing a checkpoint queue from an already-open repository launches no metadata Git subprocess.
- The Trace2 positive control runs `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and confirms that the subprocess detector records it.
- Tests preserve the required queue fail-closed and optional redaction-cache fail-open policies.
- The repository ownership guard no longer needs an exception for checkpoint metadata traversal.
- Source-built `entire status` passed.
- Source-built `entire doctor` reported metadata branches and hooks as healthy; it also found two pre-existing ended sessions awaiting condensation, unrelated to this diff.

No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

## Deliberately not included

This PR does not migrate session, strategy, hook, or other product consumers. Those areas have separate migrations so their error handling, fallback behavior, and performance-sensitive paths can be reviewed independently.

It also does not redesign checkpoint persistence, change ref formats, alter queue semantics, add cross-worktree writes, or replace genuine Git queries for refs, objects, configuration, and repository semantics.

{"body":"Refs #2052, particularly [the duplicate-traversal finding](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2052#issuecomment-5400538888) and [the follow-up commitment](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2052#issuecomment-5429341093).

PR #2052 exposed that several packages independently interpreted `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree identity. Those implementations had already diverged on layouts such as bare containers, linked worktrees, and submodules, while session and checkpoint maintained separate caches for answers derived from the same filesystem metadata.

This consolidates those physical Git facts under the existing `gitrepo` ownership boundary and removes the duplicate traversal and cache layers.

## Why this touches 67 files

This is one ownership change with a wide dependency graph, not 67 separate features.

Before this change, checkpoint, session, strategy, settings, status, review,
investigate, trail, setup/cleanup, and Codex independently interpreted some
combination of `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree identity:

```text
Before

checkpoint ─┐
session ────┤
strategy ───┤ each resolves Git metadata independently
settings ───┤ and some cache the result separately
status ─────┤
review ─────┤
Codex ──────┘

After

                    gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata
                                  │
              ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
           checkpoint          session            strategy...
```

The 67 changed files break down into 37 production files and 30 test files:

| Area | Files | Why they changed |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Canonical `gitrepo` owner | 7 | Add the resolver, repository-opening boundary, tests, and ownership guard |
| Checkpoint migration | 7 | Remove its common-directory cache and migrate consumers |
| Session migration | 7 | Remove its separate cache and preserve adoption/sweep behavior |
| Strategy and hook paths | 18 | Migrate the hottest and most policy-sensitive consumers |
| Other product consumers | 18 | Migrate settings, status, review, investigate, trail, Codex, setup, and cleanup |
| Legacy `paths` deletion | 2 | Remove the old marker-based worktree-ID parser |
| Cross-cutting proof | 8 | Update fixtures and prove caller policy and subprocess behavior |

Most production changes are small call-site migrations. The largest additions
are tests proving real Git layouts, failure behavior, ownership boundaries, and
subprocess counts. Despite the broad footprint, production Go decreases by 36
lines.

## One owner for physical worktree metadata

`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` now resolves one explicit worktree root into:

- its per-worktree Git directory
- its common Git directory
- its optional linked-worktree ID

The resolver has no CWD lookup, Git subprocess, cache, context, options, environment interpretation, layout taxonomy, or feature-specific policy.

Returned paths remain cleaned absolute lexical paths. Physical filesystem identity is used only to determine whether the Git directory equals the common directory and whether a linked-worktree Git directory is an immediate child of `CommonDir/worktrees`.

Resolution is all-or-error. Malformed worktree metadata cannot silently downgrade into another repository-opening path, while deliberately opening a validated bare repository remains a separate `gitrepo.OpenPath` operation.

## Consolidation and deletion

All former filesystem-metadata consumers now use the canonical resolver while retaining their existing caller-owned error, warning, fallback, trust, and installation policies.

This removes:

- the session common-directory cache and its clearing behavior
- the checkpoint common-directory cache
- duplicate `.git` and `commondir` traversal
- marker-based worktree-ID parsing
- the old `paths` worktree metadata helpers
- migration wrappers that would otherwise preserve fragmented ownership

A source guard rejects new production parsing of `gitdir:`, `commondir`, or independent `.git` filesystem traversal outside `gitrepo`, with two documented policy-only exceptions.

The production Go diff is 557 additions and 593 deletions: net 36 lines removed despite adding the canonical resolver.

## Hook-path subprocess evidence

Operation-level Git tracing records these changes against the historical pre-consolidation counts:

| Operation | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Session state construction | 2 | 1 |
| Construct and enqueue through checkpoint queue | 1 | 0 |
| `prepare-commit-msg` without an active session | 4 | 2 |
| `entire status` | 4 | 3 |
| Codex hook discovery | 1 | 1 |

These values count Git subprocesses, not whether the operation still occurs. The checkpoint queue retains its locking, append, drain, and removal behavior; it now obtains the common directory through filesystem metadata resolution instead of spawning Git.

The consolidation adds no Git subprocesses and removes the filesystem-metadata `--git-common-dir` queries. The one remaining common-directory query on the prepare-commit path is retained semantic repository-identity behavior rather than metadata traversal.

## Verification

- `mise run check`
  - formatting passed
  - lint passed with 0 issues
  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed
  - Vogon canary passed 56/56
  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`
- Real Git-created fixtures cover ordinary repositories, linked worktrees, `.bare/worktrees`, bare repositories with linked worktrees, separate Git directories, ordinary and linked submodules, relative pointers, symlink aliases, and moved registrations.
- Handmade fixtures cover malformed and broken metadata.
- Tests verify caller-owned failure policies, fail-closed repository opening, common-directory/worktree-ID agreement, and physical alias identity.
- The source guard was positive-control tested by temporarily adding forbidden independent traversal and observing the expected failure.
- No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

## Deliberately unchanged

This does not change Codex backlink, ownership, trust, warning, diagnostic, or installation policy. It does not add cross-worktree writes, resolver flags, a generic Git facade, or replace genuine Git queries for refs, objects, configuration, or repository semantics.

{"body":"Refs #2190.

PR #2190 moved every Git metadata consumer at once. The review exposed two separate jobs: define one owner for the metadata, then migrate its callers.

This is split part 1. It adds the resolver and changes only repository opening. Checkpoint, session, strategy, hooks, and other consumers stay unchanged here.

## Files and ownership

Three production files and four test files change. All paths below are relative to `cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/`.

| File | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata.go` | No file | Resolves the three metadata facts |
| `repository.go` | Opening rediscovered paths | Resolves and passes metadata |
| `reftable.go` | Errors looked like absence | Returns inspection errors |
| `metadata_guard_test.go` | No guard | Blocks new duplicate traversal |
| `metadata_test.go` | No resolver tests | Covers real and broken layouts |
| `repository_test.go` | Tested the old path | Covers fallback and failures |
| `reftable_test.go` | Tested boolean detection | Covers inspection errors |

The call path changes like this:

```text
Before

OpenPath
  ├── resolve .git and commondir while opening
  ├── resolve them again while checking alternates
  └── fall back without one validated metadata result

After

OpenPath
  └── ResolveWorktreeMetadata
        ├── GitDir
        ├── CommonDir
        └── WorktreeID
              │
              ├── repository storage
              ├── alternates inspection
              └── reftable inspection
```

## One resolver for three facts

`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` resolves an explicit worktree root into:

- `GitDir`
- `CommonDir`
- `WorktreeID`

The resolver takes a worktree root. It does not discover one from CWD, read Git environment variables, run Git, cache results, or choose a caller's policy.

Resolution is all-or-error. Malformed or unreadable metadata stops the open.

`gitrepo.OpenPath` now resolves metadata once and passes those facts into repository opening, object-alternates detection, and reftable inspection.

A bare-repository open is tried only when worktree metadata does not exist.

## Symlinks and `..` keep their filesystem meaning

Lexically cleaning a path through a symlink can change where `..` leads. The resolver checks filesystem identity before it returns a cleaned path.

Linked-worktree registrations may use physical aliases. They must still resolve to an immediate child of `CommonDir/worktrees`.

Inspection errors now reach the caller. They no longer mean "feature absent." This applies to reftable inspection and malformed `.git` layouts.

## Fixes a hang that is already released

`OpenPath` on `main` identifies a `.git` entry by reading it: `os.Stat`, then `os.ReadFile`. That works for a directory or a regular file. For three other entry types the read never finishes.

| `.git` is | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A FIFO with no writer | Blocks until a writer opens it | Refused on type |
| A symlink to such a FIFO | Blocks until a writer opens it | Refused on type |
| A symlink to `/dev/zero` | Reads forever, memory grows | Refused on type |

The resolver checks the type first. It opens only a directory or a regular file, and refuses anything else by name.

None of these arrive by clone. Git refuses a `.git` path component in a tree at any depth, so each one needs local write access to the worktree. This is a robustness fix, not a vulnerability.

## `gitdir:` strictness now matches Git

The legacy parser accepted pointer files that Git rejects. It cut the prefix at `gitdir:` instead of `gitdir: `, then trimmed whitespace from the remainder. That let `gitdir:target`, ` gitdir: target`, and `gitdir:\ttarget` all resolve. Git requires the single space and trims nothing.
The fixture covers seven `.git` pointer spellings. The new resolver agrees with Git on all seven. The legacy parser agreed on three.
This changes behavior. A `.git` file that worked only because Entire was more permissive than Git now fails, and every other Git tool was already failing it.

## Stop new duplicate traversal

A source guard scans production Go across the repository. It rejects new `.git`, `gitdir:`, and `commondir` traversal outside `gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata`.
The guard lists the existing callers that later PRs must migrate:

- checkpoint metadata
- session metadata
- strategy and hooks
- remaining product consumers

The exception list records each function and the one `git rev-parse` flag it may use. If that function starts using another metadata flag, the guard fails. The test also fails when a listed exception no longer exists.

A temporary multi-file repository test runs the complete scanner. It proves that the scanner follows a package constant into another file, scans production code under `internal/`, and ignores a parameter named `gitDir`.

Positive controls cover rooted filesystem APIs, package constants, `Readlink`, aliased imports, and legacy resolver calls.

## Verification

- `mise run check`
  - formatting passed
  - lint passed with 0 issues
  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed
  - Vogon canary passed 56/56
  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4
- `git diff main --check`
- Real Git fixtures cover ordinary, linked, bare, separate-Git-dir, submodule, symlink-alias, moved-registration, alternates, and reftable layouts.
- On the seven `.git` pointer spellings in the fixture, the new resolver matches Git on 7/7. The legacy parser matched 3/7.
- Broken fixtures verify fail-closed repository opening and typed absence.

No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

## Deliberately not included

Checkpoint, session, strategy, hooks, and other product consumers still use their existing paths. Separate PRs will migrate them without mixing their error and fallback policies into this resolver change. The last migration will remove the legacy resolvers.

{"body":"> **Dependency:** This PR is built on #2241 and must not merge before it. Until #2241 lands, the Files changed view includes both #2241 and this checkpoint refactor. After #2241 merges, this branch will be rebased onto `main` and force-pushed so the PR contains only the checkpoint changes.

For the checkpoint-only change before that rebase, see the [comparison against the prerequisite branch](https://github.com/MuskanPaliwal/cli/compare/refactor-git-metadata-owner...refactor-checkpoint-metadata-resolution).

Refs #2052 and #2190.

PR #2190 established the broader direction: physical Git worktree metadata should have one canonical owner instead of being rediscovered independently across the CLI. PR #2241 introduces that owner in `gitrepo` and migrates repository opening. This PR follows it by moving the checkpoint subsystem onto the canonical metadata boundary and deleting checkpoint's duplicate traversal and caching implementation.

This is intended as an ownership refactor rather than a checkpoint behavior change. Queue placement, redaction caching, persistent refs, shadow refs, locking, and caller-specific failure policies remain intact.

## Broader refactor

Checkpoint operations need to know both the current worktree root and the repository's common Git directory. The common directory determines where repository-wide state such as the push queue and redaction cache belongs, particularly when a command runs from a linked worktree.

Before this change, checkpoint resolved that metadata itself:

```text
Checkpoint operation
        │
        ▼
checkpoint.resolveGitCommonDir
        │
        ├── git rev-parse --git-common-dir
        ├── package-level mutex
        └── per-worktree cache
```

That made checkpoint a second owner of the same physical Git facts already being consolidated under `gitrepo`. It also gave checkpoint its own cache lifecycle, cancellation-dependent behavior, and subprocess cost.

After this change, checkpoint starts from the already-open repository and delegates physical metadata resolution to the canonical owner:

```text
Checkpoint operation
        │
        ▼
checkpoint.repositoryDirs
        │
        ▼
gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata
        │
        ├── Worktree root
        ├── Per-worktree Git directory
        └── Common Git directory
```

The checkpoint package retains a small adapter because checkpoint callers commonly need the worktree root and common directory together. Interpretation of `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree layout remains owned exclusively by `gitrepo`.

## Why remove the checkpoint cache

The deleted cache was compensating for a Git subprocess rather than caching an expensive domain object. Once metadata resolution becomes rooted filesystem inspection, the cache no longer provides a useful ownership boundary.

Removing it has three useful consequences:

- An already-open repository no longer launches `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` when constructing checkpoint state.
- Repairs to `.git` or `commondir` metadata are observed by the next operation instead of remaining hidden behind a stale cached result.
- Checkpoint no longer owns a mutex, cache-clearing API, or cancellation-dependent cache semantics for facts owned by `gitrepo`.

This also removes the checkpoint-specific resolver and its cache-only tests.

## Checkpoint consumers moved to the canonical boundary

The migration covers the checkpoint paths that depend on repository metadata:

- rooted push-queue construction
- redaction-cache placement
- persistent ref updates
- ref-store construction
- ephemeral checkpoint storage
- shadow-ref operations
- file-lock placement

These consumers now receive metadata from the same resolver used when opening the repository, without introducing a generic Git facade or moving checkpoint-specific policy into `gitrepo`.

## Caller policy remains local

The canonical resolver reports metadata facts and errors; it does not decide whether an individual checkpoint feature is required or optional.

That distinction remains deliberate:

- Push-queue construction fails closed because enqueueing against the wrong repository directory could lose or misdirect required work.
- Redaction caching fails open because caching is an optimization and transcript redaction can continue without it.
- Persistent ref updates retain their existing locking, compare-and-swap conflict handling, retry, and cancellation behavior.
- Linked worktrees continue sharing repository-wide state through the common Git directory.
- Shadow refs and ephemeral checkpoint data retain their existing worktree-specific placement.

## Observable effect

No user-facing command or checkpoint format changes.

The operational effect is narrower:

- checkpoint metadata lookup no longer launches a Git subprocess for an already-open repository
- checkpoint metadata is no longer memoized independently from the filesystem
- malformed metadata continues to follow each caller's existing required or optional failure policy
- ordinary repositories and linked worktrees retain their existing storage locations

The checkpoint-only layer relative to #2241 contains 16 files, with 139 additions and 211 deletions. Most additions are focused behavioral tests; the production change primarily removes duplicate traversal and cache machinery.

## Verification

- `mise run check`
  - formatting passed
  - lint passed with 0 issues
  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed
  - Vogon canary passed 56/56
  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4
- Pre-PR `mise run lint` passed with 0 issues.
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check` passed.
- A real linked-worktree fixture proves that its queue is stored in the main repository's common Git directory.
- A repair test proves that corrected metadata is observed immediately without clearing a cache.
- A Git Trace2 test proves that constructing a checkpoint queue from an already-open repository launches no metadata Git subprocess.
- The Trace2 positive control runs `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and confirms that the subprocess detector records it.
- Tests preserve the required queue fail-closed and optional redaction-cache fail-open policies.
- The repository ownership guard no longer needs an exception for checkpoint metadata traversal.
- Source-built `entire status` passed.
- Source-built `entire doctor` reported metadata branches and hooks as healthy; it also found two pre-existing ended sessions awaiting condensation, unrelated to this diff.

No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

## Deliberately not included

This PR does not migrate session, strategy, hook, or other product consumers. Those areas have separate migrations so their error handling, fallback behavior, and performance-sensitive paths can be reviewed independently.

It also does not redesign checkpoint persistence, change ref formats, alter queue semantics, add cross-worktree writes, or replace genuine Git queries for refs, objects, configuration, and repository semantics.

{"body":"Refs #2052, particularly [the duplicate-traversal finding](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2052#issuecomment-5400538888) and [the follow-up commitment](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2052#issuecomment-5429341093).

PR #2052 exposed that several packages independently interpreted `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree identity. Those implementations had already diverged on layouts such as bare containers, linked worktrees, and submodules, while session and checkpoint maintained separate caches for answers derived from the same filesystem metadata.

This consolidates those physical Git facts under the existing `gitrepo` ownership boundary and removes the duplicate traversal and cache layers.

## Why this touches 67 files

This is one ownership change with a wide dependency graph, not 67 separate features.

Before this change, checkpoint, session, strategy, settings, status, review,
investigate, trail, setup/cleanup, and Codex independently interpreted some
combination of `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree identity:

```text
Before

checkpoint ─┐
session ────┤
strategy ───┤ each resolves Git metadata independently
settings ───┤ and some cache the result separately
status ─────┤
review ─────┤
Codex ──────┘

After

                    gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata
                                  │
              ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
           checkpoint          session            strategy...
```

The 67 changed files break down into 37 production files and 30 test files:

| Area | Files | Why they changed |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Canonical `gitrepo` owner | 7 | Add the resolver, repository-opening boundary, tests, and ownership guard |
| Checkpoint migration | 7 | Remove its common-directory cache and migrate consumers |
| Session migration | 7 | Remove its separate cache and preserve adoption/sweep behavior |
| Strategy and hook paths | 18 | Migrate the hottest and most policy-sensitive consumers |
| Other product consumers | 18 | Migrate settings, status, review, investigate, trail, Codex, setup, and cleanup |
| Legacy `paths` deletion | 2 | Remove the old marker-based worktree-ID parser |
| Cross-cutting proof | 8 | Update fixtures and prove caller policy and subprocess behavior |

Most production changes are small call-site migrations. The largest additions
are tests proving real Git layouts, failure behavior, ownership boundaries, and
subprocess counts. Despite the broad footprint, production Go decreases by 36
lines.

## One owner for physical worktree metadata

`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` now resolves one explicit worktree root into:

- its per-worktree Git directory
- its common Git directory
- its optional linked-worktree ID

The resolver has no CWD lookup, Git subprocess, cache, context, options, environment interpretation, layout taxonomy, or feature-specific policy.

Returned paths remain cleaned absolute lexical paths. Physical filesystem identity is used only to determine whether the Git directory equals the common directory and whether a linked-worktree Git directory is an immediate child of `CommonDir/worktrees`.

Resolution is all-or-error. Malformed worktree metadata cannot silently downgrade into another repository-opening path, while deliberately opening a validated bare repository remains a separate `gitrepo.OpenPath` operation.

## Consolidation and deletion

All former filesystem-metadata consumers now use the canonical resolver while retaining their existing caller-owned error, warning, fallback, trust, and installation policies.

This removes:

- the session common-directory cache and its clearing behavior
- the checkpoint common-directory cache
- duplicate `.git` and `commondir` traversal
- marker-based worktree-ID parsing
- the old `paths` worktree metadata helpers
- migration wrappers that would otherwise preserve fragmented ownership

A source guard rejects new production parsing of `gitdir:`, `commondir`, or independent `.git` filesystem traversal outside `gitrepo`, with two documented policy-only exceptions.

The production Go diff is 557 additions and 593 deletions: net 36 lines removed despite adding the canonical resolver.

## Hook-path subprocess evidence

Operation-level Git tracing records these changes against the historical pre-consolidation counts:

| Operation | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Session state construction | 2 | 1 |
| Construct and enqueue through checkpoint queue | 1 | 0 |
| `prepare-commit-msg` without an active session | 4 | 2 |
| `entire status` | 4 | 3 |
| Codex hook discovery | 1 | 1 |

These values count Git subprocesses, not whether the operation still occurs. The checkpoint queue retains its locking, append, drain, and removal behavior; it now obtains the common directory through filesystem metadata resolution instead of spawning Git.

The consolidation adds no Git subprocesses and removes the filesystem-metadata `--git-common-dir` queries. The one remaining common-directory query on the prepare-commit path is retained semantic repository-identity behavior rather than metadata traversal.

## Verification

- `mise run check`
  - formatting passed
  - lint passed with 0 issues
  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed
  - Vogon canary passed 56/56
  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`
- Real Git-created fixtures cover ordinary repositories, linked worktrees, `.bare/worktrees`, bare repositories with linked worktrees, separate Git directories, ordinary and linked submodules, relative pointers, symlink aliases, and moved registrations.
- Handmade fixtures cover malformed and broken metadata.
- Tests verify caller-owned failure policies, fail-closed repository opening, common-directory/worktree-ID agreement, and physical alias identity.
- The source guard was positive-control tested by temporarily adding forbidden independent traversal and observing the expected failure.
- No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

## Deliberately unchanged

This does not change Codex backlink, ownership, trust, warning, diagnostic, or installation policy. It does not add cross-worktree writes, resolver flags, a generic Git facade, or replace genuine Git queries for refs, objects, configuration, or repository semantics.

use canonical Git metadata resolution (split part 2)\"}\n{\"body\":\"Refs #2052, particularly [the duplicate-traversal finding](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2052#issuecomment-5400538888) and [the follow-up commitment](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2052#issuecomment-5429341093).\\n\\nPR #2052 exposed that several packages independently interpreted `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree identity. Those implementations had already diverged on layouts such as bare containers, linked worktrees, and submodules, while session and checkpoint maintained separate caches for answers derived from the same filesystem metadata.\\n\\nThis consolidates those physical Git facts under the existing `gitrepo` ownership boundary and removes the duplicate traversal and cache layers.\\n\\n## Why this touches 67 files\\n\\nThis is one ownership change with a wide dependency graph, not 67 separate features.\\n\\nBefore this change, checkpoint, session, strategy, settings, status, review,\\ninvestigate, trail, setup/cleanup, and Codex independently interpreted some\\ncombination of `.git`, `gitdir:`, `commondir`, and linked-worktree identity:\\n\\n```text\\nBefore\\n\\ncheckpoint ─┐\\nsession ────┤\\nstrategy ───┤ each resolves Git metadata independently\\nsettings ───┤ and some cache the result separately\\nstatus ─────┤\\nreview ─────┤\\nCodex ──────┘\\n\\nAfter\\n\\n                    gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata\\n                                  │\\n              ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐\\n           checkpoint          session            strategy...\\n```\\n\\nThe 67 changed files break down into 37 production files and 30 test files:\\n\\n| Area | Files | Why they changed |\\n| --- | ---: | --- |\\n| Canonical `gitrepo` owner | 7 | Add the resolver, repository-opening boundary, tests, and ownership guard |\\n| Checkpoint migration | 7 | Remove its common-directory cache and migrate consumers |\\n| Session migration | 7 | Remove its separate cache and preserve adoption/sweep behavior |\\n| Strategy and hook paths | 18 | Migrate the hottest and most policy-sensitive consumers |\\n| Other product consumers | 18 | Migrate settings, status, review, investigate, trail, Codex, setup, and cleanup |\\n| Legacy `paths` deletion | 2 | Remove the old marker-based worktree-ID parser |\\n| Cross-cutting proof | 8 | Update fixtures and prove caller policy and subprocess behavior |\\n\\nMost production changes are small call-site migrations. The largest additions\\nare tests proving real Git layouts, failure behavior, ownership boundaries, and\\nsubprocess counts. Despite the broad footprint, production Go decreases by 36\\nlines.\\n\\n## One owner for physical worktree metadata\\n\\n`gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata` now resolves one explicit worktree root into:\\n\\n- its per-worktree Git directory\\n- its common Git directory\\n- its optional linked-worktree ID\\n\\nThe resolver has no CWD lookup, Git subprocess, cache, context, options, environment interpretation, layout taxonomy, or feature-specific policy.\\n\\nReturned paths remain cleaned absolute lexical paths. Physical filesystem identity is used only to determine whether the Git directory equals the common directory and whether a linked-worktree Git directory is an immediate child of `CommonDir/worktrees`.\\n\\nResolution is all-or-error. Malformed worktree metadata cannot silently downgrade into another repository-opening path, while deliberately opening a validated bare repository remains a separate `gitrepo.OpenPath` operation.\\n\\n## Consolidation and deletion\\n\\nAll former filesystem-metadata consumers now use the canonical resolver while retaining their existing caller-owned error, warning, fallback, trust, and installation policies.\\n\\nThis removes:\\n\\n- the session common-directory cache and its clearing behavior\\n- the checkpoint common-directory cache\\n- duplicate `.git` and `commondir` traversal\\n- marker-based worktree-ID parsing\\n- the old `paths` worktree metadata helpers\\n- migration wrappers that would otherwise preserve fragmented ownership\\n\\nA source guard rejects new production parsing of `gitdir:`, `commondir`, or independent `.git` filesystem traversal outside `gitrepo`, with two documented policy-only exceptions.\\n\\nThe production Go diff is 557 additions and 593 deletions: net 36 lines removed despite adding the canonical resolver.\\n\\n## Hook-path subprocess evidence\\n\\nOperation-level Git tracing records these changes against the historical pre-consolidation counts:\\n\\n| Operation | Before | After |\\n| --- | ---: | ---: |\\n| Session state construction | 2 | 1 |\\n| Construct and enqueue through checkpoint queue | 1 | 0 |\\n| `prepare-commit-msg` without an active session | 4 | 2 |\\n| `entire status` | 4 | 3 |\\n| Codex hook discovery | 1 | 1 |\\n\\nThese values count Git subprocesses, not whether the operation still occurs. The checkpoint queue retains its locking, append, drain, and removal behavior; it now obtains the common directory through filesystem metadata resolution instead of spawning Git.\\n\\nThe consolidation adds no Git subprocesses and removes the filesystem-metadata `--git-common-dir` queries. The one remaining common-directory query on the prepare-commit path is retained semantic repository-identity behavior rather than metadata traversal.\\n\\n## Verification\\n\\n- `mise run check`\\n  - formatting passed\\n  - lint passed with 0 issues\\n  - race-enabled unit and integration tests passed\\n  - Vogon canary passed 56/56\\n  - external deterministic canary passed 4/4\\n- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`\\n- Real Git-created fixtures cover ordinary repositories, linked worktrees, `.bare/worktrees`, bare repositories with linked worktrees, separate Git directories, ordinary and linked submodules, relative pointers, symlink aliases, and moved registrations.\\n- Handmade fixtures cover malformed and broken metadata.\\n- Tests verify caller-owned failure policies, fail-closed repository opening, common-directory/worktree-ID agreement, and physical alias identity.\\n- The source guard was positive-control tested by temporarily adding forbidden independent traversal and observing the expected failure.\\n- No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.\\n\\n## Deliberately unchanged\\n\\nThis does not change Codex backlink, ownership, trust, warning, diagnostic, or installation policy. It does not add cross-worktree writes, resolver flags, a generic Git facade, or replace genuine Git queries for refs, objects, configuration, or repository semantics.\\n\",\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"title\":\"refactor(gitrepo): consolidate worktree metadata traversal\"}\n[{\"conclusion\":\"success\",\"databaseId\":33949641669,\"headSha\":\"61dac01ed02a40a3537f5896021d3db288b32ced\",\"name\":\"Nightly Release\",\"status\":\"completed\"},{\"conclusion\":\"success\",\"databaseId\":33905550730,\"headSha\":\"61dac01ed02a40a3537f5896021d3db288b32ced\",\"name\":\"github_actions in / for github/codeql-action/init, github/codeql-action/analyze - Update #1557861719\",\"status\":\"completed\"},{\"conclusion\":\"success\",\"databaseId\":33905550451,\"headSha\":\"61dac01ed02a40a3537f5896021d3db288b32ced\",\"name\":\"go_modules in / for github.com/gofrs/flock, github.com/posthog/posthog-go - Update #1557861716\",\"status\":\"completed\"},{\"conclusion\":\"success\",\"databaseId\":33905550059,\"headSha\":\"61dac01ed02a40a3537f5896021d3db288b32ced\",\"name\":\"github_actions in /. - Update #1557861709\",\"status\":\"completed\"},{\"conclusion\":\"success\",\"databaseId\":33905549581,\"headSha\":\"61dac01ed02a40a3537f5896021d3db288b32ced\",\"name\":\"go_modules in /. - Update #1557861708\",\"status\":\"completed\"}]\n"}
